questions.question: What does `[10, 9, 1, 100].sort()` return in JavaScript?
options: It throws because no comparator was given
questions.explanation: Without a comparator, sort converts elements to strings and compares them lexicographically, so "100" comes before "9". Use `(a, b) => a - b` for numbers.

questions.question: In the six-step routine, which step should come before writing any code?
options: Understanding the problem and working small examples by hand
Writing the most optimised solution you know
Measuring the running time with performance.now()
questions.explanation: Restating the problem, clarifying edge cases and working examples by hand come first. Skipping this is the most common reason candidates solve the wrong problem.

questions.question: Why does `Array(3).fill([])` cause bugs when building a 2D grid?
options: It creates three empty slots that cannot be written to
All three slots hold the same array object, so pushing into one row changes every row
questions.explanation: fill() puts the same reference in every slot. Use `Array.from({ length: 3 }, () => [])` to create a separate array per row.

questions.question: A `maxPrice` function starts with `let best = 0`. Which test case exposes the bug?
questions.explanation: With all negative values, no element beats 0, so the function wrongly returns 0. Initialising with the first element fixes it.
